'''''Podocarpus salignus''''', the '''willow-leaf podocarp''',<ref name = RHSPF/> is a species of [[conifer]] in podocarp family [[Podocarpaceae]].  It is found only in Chile, from 35–42° south latitude, where it is threatened by [[habitat loss]].  In Chile it is known as ''Mañío de hojas largas'' (long-leaved).

== Description ==
Podocarpus salignus is a [[species]] of coniferous [[evergreen]] that reaches up to {{convert|20|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} in height and {{convert|1|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} in diameter, the [[trunk (botany)|trunk]] is straight and cylindrical, with reddish-gray [[Bark (botany)|bark]]. The arching branches bear long, narrow, willow-like leaves, and red fleshy oval fruits where male and female plants are grown together.

==Cultivation and uses==
This tree is grown in gardens and parks of Chile, and has been introduced to the British Isles. It requires heavy rainfalls or high humidity, but withstands temperatures down to {{convert|-25|C|F|abbr=on}}.<ref>Huxley. A. The New RHS Dictionary of Gardening. 1992. MacMillan Press 1992 {{ISBN|0-333-47494-5}}</ref> It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Podocarpus salignus''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/13364/Podocarpus-salignus/Details | access-date = 6 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 80 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 7 May 2018}}</ref>

The wood is of good quality, yellowish colored, straight grained, and highly moisture resistant. It is used in furniture and construction.
